case.case_title: Jayakody v. Karunanayake, Officer-in-Charge, Police Station, Polgahawela and Attorney-General
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1994] 2 Sri LR 264

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was discriminated against on the ground of political opinion in violation of Article 12(2) during the election campaign and arrest.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that he was discriminated against because of his political opinion and support for the Independent Group, as evidenced by obstruction of his campaign and arrest without warrant.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondent denied discrimination, arguing the petitioner was not entitled to special rights as he was not the official leader or candidate, and that the arrest was based on information about illegal conduct.
key_facts: Petitioner supported the Independent Group against the U.N.P. in 1991 elections.
Petitioner was arrested without warrant for alleged transport of voters, a non-cognizable offence.
Other political party members campaigned freely while petitioner’s campaign was obstructed.
Petitioner alleged discrimination based on political opinion under Article 12(2).
Court found no established discrimination on political opinion grounds.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(2) as prohibiting discrimination on specified grounds including political opinion, but held that the petitioner’s status as a supporter without official leadership or candidacy did not entitle him to special protection or exemption from lawful police action.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found no evidence that the petitioner was discriminated against on the basis of political opinion. The petitioner’s arrest was unlawful due to procedural defects but not because of discriminatory intent. The obstruction claims were not substantiated by independent evidence.
principles_established: Article 12(2) prohibits discrimination on political opinion but requires proof of such discrimination.
Supporters of political groups do not have the same rights as official leaders or candidates under Article 12(2).
Unlawful police action does not necessarily equate to discrimination under Article 12(2).

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s rights under Article 12(2) were not infringed.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was directly relevant to the petitioner’s claim of discrimination based on political opinion, but the court found no material evidence to support such discrimination in the treatment of the petitioner.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court noted the petitioner was a strong supporter but not the official leader, and that no affidavits or evidence from other group members supported claims of discrimination on political opinion grounds.
